master.one_liner: Treat two sources as a complex field and use its winding: forked zebra stripes, spiral waves, or liquid-crystal brushes, all without atan2.
master.look:
Tested in 2D. Carrier mode reads as real zebra hide: parallel, constant-width stripes with isolated forks, and fork density set by the frequency of A and B. Spiral mode resembles Belousov-Zhabotinsky chemical waves or marbling with small spiral cores. Schlieren mode gives black and white brushes meeting at point defects, like nematic liquid-crystal micrographs, and is unlike anything on the contact sheet. Uses: animal hides, wood, sci-fi textures, masks. In 3D the zeros of z are lines, so spirals become scroll waves around filaments (not rendered).
[PhaseCharge, volumetric-3d4d] Prototyped. m=3, k=0 in 2D: black and white star pinwheels at vortices with cusp lines between opposite charges, clearly unlike anything on the sheet. m=3, k=14 in 3D isosurface: tight rolled and folded sheets like pastry, ammonite or cortical folds, very unusual. m=1 with large k looks like marble bands, close to a warped PingPong, so charge is what gives the distinctive look. Use for alien organics, fungus gills, spiral chemical waves, plasma, animated textures.
[CarrierStripes, dcc-tools] Zebra, fingerprints, sand ripples, tiger stripes, corduroy with defects, wood figure, combed hair. Defect Scale sets fork density: 0.3 gives few forks, 1.2 gives broken dashes. Warp 2.5-5 gives fingerprint whorls. Good as a mask or displacement. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=25.
master.algorithm:
Inputs: A, B (one Source at seed and seed+1, or two sources), Carrier (hybrid phase), Charge (int q), Radial Frequency f, Softening eps.
a=A(p); b=B(p); r2=a*a+b*b; inv=InvSqrt(r2+eps*eps); c=a*inv; s=b*inv.
Repeat q-1 times (constant loop): (c,s)=(C*c-S*s, C*s+S*c), where (C,S) is the unit value from the first step. This gives cos(q*theta), sin(q*theta) with no atan2.
r=Sqrt(r2); phi=Carrier(p)+f*r.
Out = Cos(phi)*c - Sin(phi)*s, which equals cos(phi+q*theta).
Presets: Carrier=k*dot(dir,p), f=0 gives parallel stripes with forks at each zero of z. Carrier=0, f=25-45 gives spiral waves. Carrier=0, f=0, q=2, out=c*c gives schlieren brushes. Not normalised, a*cos(phi)-b*sin(phi) gives wave packets (single-sideband mix). Clock mode: quantise the angle into 4 or 8 sectors from sign(a), sign(b) and |a|>|b|, which needs no atan.

[ComplexPhase, signal-phase] re = A(p), im = B(p) (B may default to A with Seed Offset +1). r = sqrt(re^2+im^2+eps^2). theta = atan2approx(im, re): a = min(|re|,|im|)/max(|re|,|im|), poly r(a) = a*(0.99997 + a^2*(-0.3258 + 0.0808 a^2)) (or the 5-term version), then Select(|im|>|re|, pi/2 - r, r), Select(re<0, pi - r, r), Select(im<0, -r, r). Mode enum: Phase = theta/pi; Harmonic = cos(m*theta) (int m); UnitRe = re/r, UnitIm = im/r (phase-only noise: constant-amplitude, pinched at zeros); HalfCos/HalfSin = normalize((1+re/r, im/r)) components (line field for fingerprints); LogMag = log(r) remapped (poles at joint zeros); Winding mask = smoothstep on r (marks vortex cores as dots).
master.why_new: Stripes with point defects cannot be built from existing nodes: there is no phase carrier, and no way to add topological charge without atan2. It is the first node where the zero set of a complex field is the design control. The fork count follows from the source frequency instead of being a side effect.
master.simd_plan: Fully branch free and dimension agnostic because everything flows through sources, so 2D, 3D and 4D use the same code. Cost: 2 source evals, plus one InvSqrt, one Sqrt, one Sin+Cos, and 2 multiplies per extra charge. No lattice window of its own. Estimated (not measured) 2.5-3.5x Perlin when A and B are Perlin, far below CellularDistance in 3D and 4D.
master.continuity: C0 everywhere when eps>0 (numerically verified in the spiral preset: step ratio 8.0). At eps=0 there are isolated point discontinuities at the vortex cores. The clock mode is discontinuous by design.
master.params: Hybrid: Carrier, Radial Frequency, Softening. Members: A, B (GeneratorSource), Charge (int). Mode enum: Phase, Schlieren, Clock, Quadrature.
master.risks:
Spirals have non-constant width because |grad r| varies, so they look like sine-of-noise away from the cores; combining with IsoBands distance could tighten this. Charge 1 and 2 look nearly the same at spiral preset scale. In GenTileable a linear carrier wraps on the 4D torus and stripes curve and chirp. 3D was not look-tested.
[CarrierStripes, dcc-tools] Single global orientation unless warped, and warps change local spacing. GenTileable puts a plane wave on the 4D torus, so tiled stripes curve (seamless, but direction is lost). Seed only changes S,T, not stripe direction.
[PhaseCharge, volumetric-3d4d] Band frequency depends on |grad r|, so wavelength is not constant. r range depends on the sources, so k needs normalisation. Thin cusp lines at m>=3 alias at low resolution; raise e to soften. A bit stylised for terrain.
master.cost_note: Estimated (not measured) 2.5-3.5x Perlin when A and B are Perlin, far below CellularDistance in 3D and 4D.
master.variant_notes: One formula: cos(phi + q*arg(a+ib)) from two sources. CarrierStripes is the plane-carrier q=1 preset (fingerprint and zebra forks), PhaseCharge the charge and radial-winding preset (3D scroll-wave sheets), ComplexPhase adds raw phase, log-magnitude and half-angle outputs.

master.one_liner: Phasor-style constant-contrast stripes on a Perlin corner lattice with no atan2: labyrinths, tiger stripes and fingerprints from one orientation input.
master.look: Tested. With an orientation field and cell=1.5 wavelengths, the result is tiger or fingerprint-like constant-width stripes with natural forks and chevrons, and this was the cleanest fingerprint look of everything tried. Larger cells (3.75 wavelengths) break into chopped stripe domains with seams. Random orientation per corner gives zebra camouflage patches. Orientation from the gradient of a potential makes stripes follow contours, with starbursts at critical points.
master.algorithm:
Cell=q*wavelength, with q about 1.5. For each of the 2^D corners c: h=hash(c); ang=Orientation(p)+(rnd(h)-0.5)*Spread when Orientation is connected, else ang from the hash; dir=(cos,sin)(ang); ph=k*dot(dir,p-c)+rnd2(h)*2pi. Weight w=product of quintic fades, as in Value noise.
re=sum(w*Cos(ph)); im=sum(w*Sin(ph)).
Out=re*InvSqrt(re*re+im*im+eps*eps), which equals cos(arg z).
Wave shapes: run the unit (re,im)/|z| through a charge loop for harmonics; a tri or saw needs a polynomial atan.

[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Dir=Hybrid direction, normalised (source is angle, or two sources in 3D). Lattice form: for each of 2^D corners: phi=2*pi*(r1+freq*(dir.(f-corner))); weight=product of quintic fade; (C,S)+=weight*(cos phi,sin phi). Phase=atan2(S,C) (or normalised C with floor max(|(C,S)|,0.2)). Ripple profile: ph=Phase/(2*pi)+0.5; out=ph/asym for ph<asym, else (1-ph)/(1-asym), where asym is the windward fraction. The published Phacelle form uses a 4x4 window, jitter*0.5, weight max(exp(-2 d^2)-0.01111,0), and shared orientation; Phasor noise uses per-kernel orientations and far more kernels.
master.why_new: Phase-only output at a fixed wavelength has no equivalent on the sheet. Compared with published phasor noise, it replaces sparse Gabor impulses with a dense corner lattice and replaces atan2 with Re/|z|, making it Perlin-shaped in cost and structure. Orientation is sampled at the current position, so any noise steers it.
master.simd_plan:
Branch free. Window is 2^D corners, 4 / 8 / 16. Each corner: hash, one Sin+Cos of orientation (shared when Spread=0), one Sin+Cos of phase. Estimated 2-4x Perlin in 2D and similar in 3D and 4D; not measured. 3D needs two orientation angles or a director from 3 sources, and normalised gives lamellae.
[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Lattice form: 4 sincos in 2D, about 3.5 ns plus source (3x Perlin); 8 in 3D, about 7 ns; 16 in 4D, about 14 ns. Published 4x4 form: 16 sincos, about 16 ns in 2D, and 64 in 3D, so it is unattractive above 2D. Add FS atan2 for the profile, or use the two components directly.
master.continuity: C0 with eps>0, verified numerically (ratio 8.3). With eps=0 there are point discontinuities at phasor zeros (forks). Sampling Orientation at p means the local phase gradient includes a term proportional to |p-c|*grad(theta), bounded by the cell size.
master.params: Hybrid: Orientation, Spread, Wavelength (Frequency), eps. Float: Cell/Wavelength ratio. Source is optional.
master.risks:
Wavelength fluctuates near fork chains and where Orientation changes quickly. Some square-lattice imprint in orientation domains could appear with random orientation; FFT not inspected. Stripes on the 4D torus for GenTileable project random 4D directions into a 2D tangent, so the observed wavelength varies per corner. Overlaps with a phasor noise node if another lens proposes it: keep whichever is cheaper.
[OrientedStripes, nature-phenomena] Lattice form has defect positions tied to the integer lattice and no frequency guarantees. An FFT comparison with the 4x4 form was not run. Hybrid frequency changes phase coherence and may stretch stripes. Direction fields with singularities give abrupt changes.
sources: Tricard et al. 2019, Procedural Phasor Noise (from memory, not consulted)
master.cost_note: Estimated 2-4x Perlin in 2D and similar in 3D and 4D; not measured.
master.variant_notes: OrientedStripes is the same 2^D corner lattice and contributes the asymmetric ripple profile.

transverse-dunes.look: Relief at hscale 25 reads as a transverse dune field: long ridges perpendicular to the wind, gentle lit stoss face, dark slip face, Y junctions where dunes merge, fine ripples on the windward face only, tips tapering at amplitude dips. Without coherent anchoring the lattice showed rectangular blocky dune breaks at defect <= .5; with coh the defect sweep goes cleanly from perfect ridges (.25) to junctions (.5) to broken dashes (1). Splat 3x3 kernel version is only marginally more sinuous. master.one_liner: Dune field from a phasor-style stripe phase field: an asymmetric stoss/slip-face waveform applied to the phase, amplitude dips at phase defects taper the dune ends, and small ripples ride on the stoss face only.
master.look: Long sinuous transverse ridges perpendicular to the wind with Y-junction defects, a broad gently lit windward face and a narrow dark slip face, dune tips tapering at defects, fine ripples only on the windward side. Prototyped: Dunes (c0 7.9, scalar 8.7x Perlin). Different from any stripe pattern the library can make: SineWave + warp gives symmetric profiles and no defects.
master.algorithm: Wind angle W (hybrid, so direction can vary across the map), Frequency f, Defect strength. Lattice 3x3: for each cell j with point c_j and hash h_j: orientation a_j = W + Defect*0.35*rnd11(h_j); wave vector k_j = 2*pi*f*(cos a_j, sin a_j); gaussian g_j = exp(-2.5*|p-c_j|^2); phase phi_j = dot(k_j, p-c_j) + Defect*2*pi*rnd01(h_j). re = sum g_j cos phi_j, im = sum g_j sin phi_j; amp = sqrt(re^2+im^2); phase theta = atan2(im,re)/(2*pi) in [0,1) (polynomial atan2 in the port, 1e-3 accuracy is plenty since the profile is piecewise linear). Dune profile: prof = theta < Stoss ? theta/Stoss : (1-theta)/(1-Stoss) (Stoss ~0.8 gives a 4:1 gentle windward face to steep slip face); crest rounded by a smoothstep window if Crest Round > 0. Height = prof * sat(amp/0.8) (defects: amplitude falls to zero, dune pinches out instead of tearing). Ripples: sin(2*pi*7f*dot(w, p) + 2*noise) * Ripple * smoothstep(0,0.08,theta) * (1 - smoothstep(Stoss-0.08, Stoss, theta)) * sat(amp): ripples only on the stoss, fading at the brink. Output 2*(height+ripples)-1. 3D: use the same kernels in a 3x3x3 window with k_j in the xy-plane only (dunes extruded along z is meaningless; for 3D density terrains output the 2D value after dropping the axis closest to the wind normal). Star dunes: see PolarCells with Spokes = 3..5.
master.why_new: Dunes are defined by asymmetry and by defect topology, neither of which a graph can get from SineWave, Perlin or warps. The asymmetric waveform requires a phase, and a phase requires the complex (re, im) sum, which is internal to the node.
master.simd_plan: 9 kernels (27 in 3D) each: one Exp, one Sin+Cos (or a single sincos poly), FMAs; then Sqrt and a polynomial atan2 (~12 ops), the piecewise profile via Select, one more Sin for ripples. Estimated 2D ~4-6x Perlin, 3D ~15x. 4D: 81 kernels, possible but slow; acceptable since dunes are rarely tiled in 4D.
master.continuity: C0: the phase wraps at theta=1 where prof is 0 on both sides; amplitude multiplies out the singular point where re=im=0; ripple gates are smoothsteps. Measured c0ratio 7.91. Not C1 at the crest unless Crest Round > 0.
master.params: Wind Angle (hybrid), Frequency, Defect, Stoss Fraction, Crest Round, Ripple Amplitude, Ripple Frequency Ratio, Kernel Width.
master.risks: Gaussian kernels truncated at the 3x3 window: with Kernel Width too large a faint seam appears at cell borders (keep exp(-2.5 r^2) or tighter). Frequency must be at least ~1.5 cycles per cell or the stripes break into blobs. Dune height does not depend on dune spacing (real fields do); expose Height as hybrid.
sources: Tricard et al. 2019, Procedural Phasor Noise (phase/amplitude decomposition that this reuses; the dune profile, defect taper and stoss-gated ripples are the new part)

master.one_liner: Interference of windowed circular/spherical waves emitted from jittered lattice points, summed as a complex field: ripple rings, soap-film amplitude nets, zone plates and fringe vortices.
master.look:
Prototype: overlapping concentric targets and spirals joined by dislocations, resembling Belousov-Zhabotinsky waves, zebra, fingerprints, topographic maps, or sand ripples; with eps large, rain on a pond. Much more ordered than anything on the sheet, with stripe width nearly constant.
[WhorlPhasor, signal-phase] Tested. Each point sits in a bullseye of rings, and neighbouring ring systems meet along lines of forks and deltas, like the topology of fingerprint whorls, peacock eyes or agate. Compared with sin(k*F1) the seams become interference chains, not sharp V kinks. Stripe width is uniform. Uses: agate, eyes, ring-spot animal patterns, sci-fi panels, decorative ripples.
master.algorithm:
Same lattice, window and accumulator as PhasorNoise but each kernel is a radial wave: r = sqrt(|p-q_c|^2 + tiny); psi = 2pi*F*r + Chirp*r^2 + PhaseJitter*2pi*rnd01(h) (Chirp != 0 makes each source a Fresnel zone plate, rings tightening outward). Per-cell presence mask m_c = (rnd01(h2) < Density) folded into w (sparser emitters = fewer, cleaner ripple families). Accumulate C += w*m*cos(psi), S += w*m*sin(psi). Outputs: Real (classic overlapping ripples), Amplitude = sqrt(C^2+S^2) (destructive-interference lines form a net between emitters: soap-film / caustic web), Caustic = Amplitude^k (hybrid k), Phase (fringes with vortices), CosPhase (constant-contrast ripples), Triangle (sharp concentric ridges = dartboard terrain).

[SpiralPhasor, lit-classic] As PhasorNoise but the kernel is a spiral. For each splat: r=sqrt(|d|^2+tiny); u=(dx+i*dy)/r; sign s=+-1 from hash.
c=exp(i*(2pi*F*r+phi)) * (s>0?u:conj(u))^W, power by W complex multiplies (W is a constant int member).
Z+=w*min(1,r/r0)*c, with r0 about .1, so the singular centre has zero weight and the field stays continuous there.
Output Zi/sqrt(|Z|^2+(eps*W)^2).
3D: pick hash axis a, two orthonormal vectors e1,e2 from a table; u=(dot(d,e1)+i*dot(d,e2))/rho, rho=length of that pair; r=rho gives extruded scroll waves, r=|d| gives shell spirals. 4D: same with a hash-chosen plane.
master.why_new: Concentric structure from many centres with interference is not reachable by the current nodes: Oscillator(CellularDistance F1) gives rings but with hard Voronoi seams and no superposition; summing two cellular passes does not interfere coherently. The complex accumulation gives phase/amplitude/caustic views for free.
master.simd_plan:
Per cell: hash, sqrt, polynomial window, sin+cos (or a parabolic wave pair). 25 cells in 2D ~25-35 ns, or 9 cells at R<=1 ~10-14 ns with smaller patches. 3D 27 cells ~40 ns. 4D 81 cells ~120 ns, for tiling only. Scalar proto was 835 ns against Worley 113 at 5x5, about 7x, so treat 3x3 as the default. Exp not needed; one final InvSqrt.
[RipplePhasor, signal-phase] Identical branch-free structure to PhasorNoise plus one sqrt per cell; window options the same (2^D half-jitter is a good default because overlap of ~2 emitters already interferes). Cost ~1.1x PhasorNoise per dimension. 4D generic (hyperspherical waves) so tiling works.
master.continuity: Dislocation points where Z=0 are the only steep spots: c0ratio 1.37 at eps 0.02 (near-point jumps, by design) and 4.67 at norm=0.85 (eps about 0.17). With larger eps it is smooth. Lipschitz constant is about f/eps near zeros.

[RippleField, stamp-scatter] Small eps gives pinprick discontinuities at dislocations, and hybrid frequency sampled per lane bends rings but can create phase runaway at far distances if not applied per-feature, so sample per-feature only. master.one_liner: Each lattice site emits a windowed radial wave; the sum gives ring interference, rain on a puddle, or caustic webs, with a built-in seamless time loop.
master.look:
Concentric ring interference like LightWave Ripples and Underwater; expanding rain rings for puddle normal maps; Caustic gives thin bright pool-floor webs. Spherical shells in 3D, useful as a banded solid. Prototype: dcc_lens mode=2.
[TuringShell, nature-phenomena] Worm-like, near-uniform-width bands; higher threshold gives rounded spots with some small rings. Looks closer to brain coral and animal coats than a Simplex threshold does, as Simplex has no preferred width. At K=2 rings around seeds are visible; K=3 reads as a better labyrinth.
master.algorithm: For each cell in the 3^dim window: h=hash(cell); c=cell+jitter(h); q=(p-c)/R; r2=dot(q,q); r=Sqrt(r2); e=Max(0,1-r2)^2. Interference mode: ph=rnd(h,1)+Time*n where n is an integer speed from hash bits; w=0.6+0.8*rnd(h,2); s += e*Cos(TAU*(Frequency*w*r - ph)). Rain mode: life=Fract(Time+rnd(h,1)); u=(r-life)*Frequency; env=Exp(-0.6*u*u)*(1-life)^2*Min(1,life/0.05); s += e*env*Cos(PI*u). Density keeps a subset by hash. Output enum: Sum, or Caustic = 2*Max(0,1-|s|)^6-1.
master.why_new: No ring structures anywhere on the sheet. Modo and LightWave ship Ripples, Rain, Drip Drop and Caustic as distinct textures; none of these are reachable with cell distance plus a graph because each site needs its own phase and the waves must sum over the window. Integer speeds give a seamless loop with no 4D torus.
master.simd_plan: 3^dim loop with Sqrt and one Cos per site (rain adds one Exp; replace with a polynomial bump for speed). Time is hybrid, so it can vary per lane. Estimated 8 / 25 / 85 ns, 2x CellularDistance, 7x Perlin in 2D; justified by the look, and Density reduces visual load but not cost.
master.continuity: C1 spatially (e has zero slope at r=1); C0 at r=0 (cone point of the wave). Caustic is C0 with creases. Rain is continuous in time thanks to the fade-in factor. Measured c0ratio 7.97-7.98.

master.one_liner: Stripes with real topological defects: a phase field carrying closed dislocation loops, so stripes fork and terminate, which isolines of a scalar can never do.
master.look: Fingerprints, zebra, sand ripples, wood-ish lamellae, seafloor ridges with transform-like forks. Prototyped: clearly fingerprint-like with Y-forks and stripe endings; FFT shows the two side lobes of a stripe pattern, with defects filling the spectrum. Thresholded, it gives zebra and labyrinth masks.
master.algorithm: phase = Tau*Frequency*Phase(x), where Phase is a source, default a warped plane. Lattice: 3x3 / 3x3x3 / 2^4 round-based window. For each point with hash01 < Density: centre c (jitter), orthonormal pair n,m from a gradient table, sign s = +-1. v = x-c; un = v.n; um = v.m; us2 = |v|^2 - un^2 - um^2 (the component orthogonal to the n,m plane; 0 in 2D). dl = D0*sqrt(max(0, 1 - us2/S^2)). psi = atan2(2*dl*um, un^2 + um^2 - dl^2). This is the angle subtended by the pair at +-dl*n. It jumps exactly 2pi across the cut segment, which cos() cannot see, and it goes to 0 away from the pair. taper = 1 - smoothstep(1.3*max(D0,S), R1, |v|), so taper = 1 on the whole cut. Sum over window: Psi += s*psi*taper. Core guard: amp = min(amp, sat(core_dist/eps)), core_dist = sqrt((|un|-dl)^2 + um^2). Output amp*cos(phase + Psi). No per-point sign bookkeeping: every point is a neutral +1/-1 pair (2D) or a closed elliptical loop (3D, 4D closed surface), so nothing long-range leaks.
master.why_new: PingPong or Terrace of FBm gives isolines, and isolines of a smooth scalar only merge at saddles in X form. They cannot produce a stripe that simply ends. Phasor noise gets singularities only as uncontrolled by-products; here defect density, size and stripe direction are independent controls.
master.simd_plan: One polynomial atan2 per feature (no atan2 in FS, so add it). Estimates with 2^D corners: 4 ns in 2D (3.5x Perlin, about 1x CellularDistance), 8 ns in 3D, 16 ns in 4D. With 3^D jittered: 8, 25, 75 ns. GenT generic with dot products only.
master.continuity: C0 except at isolated core points or curves, where phase is undefined and cos stays bounded (a small pinwheel). Random-pair ratio about 10 in 2D, 3D and 4D, meaning continuous; dense scanline in 2D: 0 jumps. Requires w=1 across the whole cut disc, which margin ensures.
master.params: Frequency (hybrid), Density (hybrid via smooth gate), Core Separation D0, Loop Size S, Influence R1, Phase source or Direction plus Warp Amount.
master.risks:
The 3D XZ slice showed some sharp-looking edges near loops; verify they are cores and not cut leakage if the taper start is mis-set. Polynomial atan2 accuracy matters: the jump must be 2pi to well under 1e-3 relative or the cut becomes visible. Phase gets large with Frequency at far coords.
[DislocationStripes, nature-phenomena] A 2D slice of a 3D ring or 4D sphere shows fewer defects: the 3D slice shows some and the 4D slice nearly none at R=0.3, so 4D tiling needs larger R or density (not tested). master.one_liner: Complex Gabor splat sum whose phase is kept and whose amplitude is thrown away: constant-contrast labyrinths, zebra stripes and fingerprints, with orientation and frequency drivable per lane. Gabor Real is an Output mode of the same node.
master.look: Prototype cl_phasor: PhaseSine gives constant-amplitude worm labyrinths that threshold into Turing or reaction-diffusion mazes; Spread .15 gives zebra or fingerprint flows; a slow Angle field gives flowing wood or hair grain. GaborReal has a clean ring FFT and a flat-topped histogram. Good for reaction-diffusion masks without simulation, coral, zebra, dunes, microstructure, 3D gyroid-like volumes. Simplex window gives shorter, kinkier bars.
master.algorithm: p *= 1/FeatureScale. Window = 3^D cells around floor(p) (see simd_plan for 2^D and simplex variants). Per cell c: h = hash(seed,c); q = c + 0.5 + Jitter*(rnd01(h)-0.5) per axis; r2 = |p-q|^2; w = max(0, 1 - r2/R^2)^3 (R = 1.5, compact C2 window, no exp). Direction d_c by DirectionMode enum: Random (2D angle = 2pi*bits(h); 3D rndDir3(h); 4D rndDir4(h)); Fixed (param angles); Quantised (angle = 2pi*floor(N*u)/N, lerped with the random angle by Snap in [0,1] -> 3-fold snap = circuit traces / 2-fold = brick); Source (direction from HybridSource angle(s) sampled ONCE at p, not at q: 1 eval, kernels in one lane share a direction, phase stays continuous because d(p) is continuous); HalfAngle (fingerprint: two sources n1,n2 sampled at p, u=(n1,n2)/|n|, d = normalize((1+u.x, u.y)) with Select to (0,1) when |1+u.x|<eps; this is a LINE field whose zeros are +1/2 cores and -1/2 deltas, exactly fingerprint minutiae). Kernel phase psi = 2pi*F*dot(d_c, p-q) + PhaseJitter*2pi*rnd01(h') where F is Hybrid 'Frequency' in cycles per cell (>= ~1.5). Accumulate C += w*cos(psi), S += w*sin(psi). Output enum: Real = C/norm (Gabor look), Amplitude = sqrt(C^2+S^2)/norm, Phase = atan2approx(S,C)/pi (sawtooth), SinPhase = S/sqrt(C^2+S^2+eps^2) (the phasor: constant-contrast stripes), CosPhase = C/sqrt(..) (use this for line-field modes: even in d so flipping d->-d is invisible; PhaseJitter must be 0 there), Triangle = 1-2|Phase| (ridge cross-section, constant width = exact furrows/dunes), Pulse = smoothstep(Duty-Soft, Duty+Soft, frac(Phase)) with Hybrid Duty (PWM stripes).
master.why_new: Nothing on the contact sheet has a narrow ring spectrum or constant-contrast stripes. Perlin, Simplex and FBm are broad band blobs, SineWave is periodic. It cannot be graphed because the splat sum must stay complex until the end, and hybrids stay stable because the phase is per splat.
master.simd_plan:
Fully branch-free: masks only in Select for half-angle and octant atan. Window options as an enum: 3^D jittered (quality, 9/27/81 cells); 2^D half-jitter (q within cell centre +-0.25, window cells = floor(p-0.5)+{0,1}, R=0.75, seamless proof: excluded cells are >=0.75 away; 4/8/16 cells, coverage ~1.8 kernels/pt); Simplex corners (D+1 kernels at the skewed simplex corners, falloff (0.5-r2)^4 as Simplex: 3/4/5 kernels, cheapest, lattice-aligned dislocations). Per cell ~45 ops (hash, jitter, dot, window, sincos poly). Est. 3^D: 2D ~4x Perlin (4.5 ns), 3D ~2x CellularDistance 3D (25 ns), 4D ~2.5x CellularDistance 4D. 2^D: 2D ~2x Perlin, 3D ~2x Perlin3D, 4D ~2.5x Perlin4D. Simplex variant ~1.5x Simplex at every dimension. 4D works generically so GenTileable2D tiles.
[PhasorNoise, lit-classic] Fixed loop, masks only for w>=0. One hash: 2x10 bit jitter, 6 bit phase, 6 bit angle. Cost per splat about Cellular cell (.45 ns) plus sincos, window and accumulate (.6 ns) = ~1 ns. Window Cell3: 9/27/81 splats = ~9/28/85 ns (2D is ~8x Perlin, ~2.4x CellularDistance). Window Simplex: 3/4/5 splats = ~3/4/5 ns (~3x/2x/1.2x Perlin), the default for 3D/4D and the tiling path. Scalar prototype ratios to perlin2: 3.0 Simplex, 6.4 3x3, 7.4 4x4. Generic GenT<P...> works with a dimension-specific direction table.
master.continuity: C-infinity at eps>0 away from window edges; w reaches zero with C2 so no seams. c0ratio 7.0 for PhaseSine and 6.7 for the Simplex window. Sharp but continuous near Z=0 dislocations. Saw mode is discontinuous by design at wrap and at Z=0. 3D slice verified visually.
master.params: Feature Scale; Frequency (hybrid, cycles/cell); Jitter; PhaseJitter; DirectionMode enum; Angle (float) / Angle Source(s) (hybrid) / N snaps + Snap; Fingerprint Re/Im GeneratorSources; Output enum; Duty (hybrid), Softness; Window enum; Seed Offset.
master.risks:
Simplex window exposes triangular lattice kinks and faint lines in the FFT. Too high Frequency against a small kernel aliases into checker blobs in 3D slices. 4D Cell3 at 81 splats is impractical, so tiling relies on the Simplex window. Rapid Angle fields compress stripes; Rune Johansen reports abrupt changes in 'Simple Phacelle' where input direction changes quickly.
[PhasorNoise, signal-phase] Frequency below ~1.5 cycles/cell starves the complex sum (grey dropouts). Contrast normalisation amplifies noise where |z| small (needs eps). Source-direction mode distorts stripes slightly vs sampling at kernel centres (sampling at 9 q's would cost 9 evals). Fingerprint 3D is only an extrusion of the 2D line field. 3^D window in 4D is expensive; the 2^D window is the shipping default for 4D.

master.one_liner: Constant-contrast stripes with k-armed dislocations at phase vortices, with fractal roughness added in a way that cannot create branch cuts.
master.look: Fingerprints, zebra, labyrinth or coral with uniform contrast and k-arm forks. Rough version looks like brain coral or tiger stripes with crinkled edges. Strongly unlike Perlin's varied contrast.
master.algorithm: Complex lattice field: per lattice corner c of the 2^D cell, Z=sum over corners of fade weight w_c(p)*exp(i*(2pi*Wave*dot(g_c,p-c)+phase_c)), with g_c and phase_c from hash. Unit phasor U=Z/sqrt(|Z|^2+eps^2). Base=U^k by repeated complex multiply (k integer, no atan2). Fractal roughness: for finer octaves j with a_j<1: R=1+a_j*Z_j(p*Lac^j); multiply Base by R/|R|. |R| never reaches 0 when a_j*|Z_j|<1, so this has no winding and no branch cut, and non-integer effect is safe. Output Re(Base)+Phase rotation from a hybrid if desired. Multiplying unit phasors of different octaves directly fails: it gives white noise.
master.why_new: Phasor-style noises get constant-contrast stripes, usually via larger kernel windows; from memory Phacelle noise is the nearest relative. The k-fold defect control and the winding-free fractal phase perturbation are the additions. FastNoise has no stripe-field generator at all.

master.continuity: C-infinity with eps>0: at vortices, amplitude fades smoothly. Measured c0ratio 5.74 (k=3) and 6.37 (rough). The k power does not create cuts because k is integer.
master.params: Frequency, Wave (cycles per cell), Arms k (int), Epsilon, Rough Octaves, Rough Amount (must stay below 1), Gain, Lacunarity, Phase (hybrid).

master.look: Prototype cl_carrier steer=1,K=8,lrot=1. F=3: fine fingerprint or zebra stripes that follow the field with few dislocations, nearly the look of PhasorNoise with a field at a fraction of the kernels. Wood grain, hair, dune ripple, sediment layers that bend along a guide node.
master.algorithm:
theta=Angle(x). t=theta/pi*K; k=floor(t) mod K; f=frac(t). Use only bands k and k+1, weights cos(f*pi/2), sin(f*pi/2).
For band b: a=pi*b/K (table), w_b=(cos a,sin a). Carrier C_b=exp(i*2pi*F*dot(w_b,x)), one sincos per band per lane.
Modulator L_b(x): rotate x into the band frame q=Rot(a)*x plus a band offset, lattice cell in q, 2^d corners, quintic multilinear weights, complex coefficient from hash(seed+b*prime, corner) as two 16 bit fields mapped to [-1,1].
Z=sum_b weight_b*C_b*L_b. Output PhaseSine = Re Z/sqrt(|Z|^2+eps^2), or Gaussian = Re Z*scale.
Key point: bands are fixed fields, so varying theta only crossfades them, there is no phase shear and no swirl however fast theta varies.
3D: Axis enum (steer around X/Y/Z); or Isotropic mode with 6 icosahedral directions all evaluated. 4D: Isotropic mode with K fixed directions.
master.why_new: Driving orientation of stripes from a node is the classic open problem named in the survey (spatial variation of all noise parameters). Warp distorts spacing, and x*f(x) shears. A graph cannot do per-lane band selection with shared carriers. Cheaper than per-splat Gabor because trig is factored out of the kernel loop.
master.simd_plan: Per lane: 1 hybrid sample, k via Floor plus table permute, 2 band rotations (4 mul each), 2 sincos (~1 ns), 2x2^d hashed corners with bit field complex (~.15 ns each). Estimate 2D ~3.5 ns (3x Perlin), 3D Axis mode ~5.5 ns (2.5x), 4D ~9 ns (2x), 3D Isotropic with 6 bands ~11 ns (5x). Scalar prototype 5.2x perlin2, but it does cos/sin per corner, which the port removes.
master.continuity: C-infinity in Z (quintic lattice, continuous weights including the k wrap). Normalised output has c0ratio 3.85 with slope ~450 from sharp phase dislocations at eps=.05, which is a slope effect, not a jump; raise eps to soften. 3D form not prototyped.
master.params: Hybrid: Angle, Softness. Float: Frequency F (cycles per modulator cell; use >=2.5). Int: K (8 default). Enum: Output, Axis or Isotropic.
master.risks: Below F~2.5 boxy dislocation loops follow the rotated lattice (seen in prototype K=1 and F=1.5). Unsteered K=2 shows a grid. Isotropic use (K>=4 all active) is blobby and worse than PhasorNoise, so this node is only good steered. Ghost double stripes in crossfade zones. The theta wrap needs care when Angle is a range outside [0,pi).

master.one_liner: Argument of a rotation-invariant complex lattice field: output histogram is exactly uniform by symmetry, with true topological defects (pinwheels, spirals, forked stripes).
master.look: k=1: soft pinwheel fields with folded sheets. k=3: star junctions. c about 3: agate curls and spirals. Carrier: parallel stripes with genuine fork dislocations, as in fingerprints, zebra and wood grain. Good for marble, agate, fingerprints, bark and exact-coverage masks. Zeros are closed vortex loops in 3D. Measured coverage on the corner-phase variant: T=-0.8/-0.5/0/0.5/0.8 gives 0.9008/0.7507/0.4995/0.2511/0.1033 against targets 0.90/0.75/0.50/0.25/0.10, with the same accuracy under c=4 and carrier. XY variant: std 0.578 against 0.577 for uniform.
master.algorithm: Lattice XY model: per-corner unit phasor e^(i*phi), phi from hash. z(p) = interpolate phasors with quintic weights in the complex plane, summed over two lattices rotated about 40 degrees relative to each other to hide axes. Because all phi are iid uniform, z and e^(i*theta)*z have the same law for any weights, so arg z is exactly uniform at every point and independent of |z|. phase = k*arg(z)/tau + c*|z|^gamma + dot(Carrier, p) + Detail(p). Output tri(phase)*2 - 1 with integer k. Any term added to a uniform circle variable independent of it leaves it uniform, so spiral, carrier and independent-source detail terms all keep the histogram flat. Threshold T then covers exactly (1-T)/2 with no calibration.
master.why_new: Exact histogram with no table and no measurement, and defects are a structural property with integer charge, not a threshold artefact. Phasor and Gabor nodes need sparse convolution and do not give exact uniformity with this cheap a kernel. The graph has no atan2, so it cannot be built from existing nodes. Windowed explicit dislocation dipoles were also prototyped (25 atan2 calls, branch-cut handling); this formula replaces them with a single atan2 and no window.
master.simd_plan: Each lattice is value-noise shaped: corners 4 / 8 / 16 in 2D / 3D / 4D, two lattices. Unit phasors from a hash-indexed table or Sin/Cos. One polynomial atan2 per sample. Estimated 2-3x Perlin SIMD; scalar with std::atan2 and cos/sin measured 5x perlin2. Same code for all dimensions via GenT, 4D works so tiling works.
master.continuity: Continuous except on the zero set of z (isolated points in 2D, curves in 3D, surfaces in 4D), where all levels meet. Requires integer k. Measured c0ratio about 2.6 to 3 from those singular points.
master.params: Winding k (int), Spiral c (hybrid), Gamma (float), Carrier X/Y/Z/W (float), Detail (hybrid source), Spread (float, 1 = exact uniform; below 0.5 no vortices can form because all phases fit in a half circle, so it controls defect density but breaks exactness).
master.risks: Corners must use interpolated unit phasors. An earlier version with Perlin gradient times a phase had rank-1 zeros at lattice corners and produced visible slip faults, fixed by this form. A single lattice leaves axis bias. Defects are sharp singular points, which hillshade exposes. Without warp the carrier stays straight, so pair it with DomainWarp upstream. The 3D/4D forms are untested in the prototype.
master.cost_note: Estimated 2-3x Perlin SIMD; scalar with std::atan2 and cos/sin measured 5x perlin2.
